content:
Systematic errors are consistent, repeatable errors that can arise from environmental factors, observational biases, or instrument imperfections.  
Environmental errors (A) are one type of systematic error. Observational errors (B) due to the observer’s habits are also systematic. Instrument errors (C) from calibration or design flaws are systematic as well.  
Thus, all of the above (D) are types of systematic errors.  

Final answer: (D)
